Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. • Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills

• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic

| from 10.5 to 75.0   | http://www.hoorwa.org                        |      60 | http://www.bikereg.com//inc/content/images/EventLogos/12569.png | Bennington        | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations.  <span style="text-decoration: underline;">Post Ride Picnic:</span> Food, beverages, baked goods and more. </div>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>THE COST:</b> This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! <img src="/inc/Editor_Files/images/emsmile.gif" align="absmiddle" border="0">.)</div>  <div><br></div>  <div>Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.<br></div>  <div><br></div>  <div><br></div> | VT      | 8/20/2011  | 7th Annual Hoosic River Ride                  | http://www.bikereg.com/events/register.asp?eventid=12569 |

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The Floyd Country Store, home of the Friday Night Jamboree, was constructed around 1910, and has been an important part of the community ever since. What is still most striking in the store though, is that as people walk through the door they cant help but smile.
The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. If the crowd is willing, at 10:30pm we'll round up one of the jamming groups that can be found picking outside or upstairs in the store, and they will play for the crowd until around 11:30pm.

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Presented by the Department of Art.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

| from 10.5 to 75.0   | http://www.hoorwa.org        |      60 | http://www.bikereg.com//inc/content/images/EventLogos/12569.png | Bennington        | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations.  <span style="text-decoration: underline;">Post Ride Picnic:</span> Food, beverages, baked goods and more. </div>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>THE COST:</b> This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! <img src="/inc/Editor_Files/images/emsmile.gif" align="absmiddle" border="0">.)</div>  <div><br></div>  <div>Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.<br></div>  <div><br></div>  <div><br></div> | VT      | 8/20/2011  | 7th Annual Hoosic River Ride                  | http://www.bikereg.com/events/register.asp?eventid=12569 |

You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

A hilarious whodunit in which the audience gets a chance to solve the crime.  There's a different murderer every night so the outcome is always a mystery.   Having performed over 10,000 times in Boston, Shear Madness has been acknowledged by the Guinness Book of World Records as the longest running play in American theater history.

The New York-New York Theatre presents Zumanity, Another Side of Cirque du Soleil. Beautiful performers entice the audience with a never-before-seen blend of fashion, art, music, dance, personality and sensuality.

The show begins the moment you walk through the door into Mystery Mansion Dinner Theatre.  Welcome to Greystone Manor.  You will be given a change of identity and whisked back to Hollywood in the roaring '20s.  C.D. Weasel, hollywood's colorful producer, has invited you to his mansion for a private screening of his motion picture masterpiece "Love's Foolish Parade."  You'll meet Edward Manly III, the dashing hero...or is he?  Then there's the sweet and innocent Clara Simpleton, who couldn't be as sweet as she seems.  There is a whole cast of intriguing characters who will entertain you and even serve you dinner.  Just remember:  one or more of them is a killer!

Gotham City Improv is a comedy theater located in the heart of Chelsea, in New York City. It offers comedy shows in improvisation, sketch comedy and more! Current offerings include:  OFF THE TOP OF OUR HEADS Long-formers get back to Improv basics with short-form much like "Whose Line is it Anyway?" Winners of the Big Apple Improv Festival's Best Improv Group in NYC title. SATURDAYS at 7:00PM.  Opens run.  $7.00   Assessing Threats 101:  Turning non-threats into your worst fears FRIDAY NIGHTS @ 8:30p.m. February 18, 25   March 4, 11  GOTHAM CITY IMPROV SHOWS  Crux brings the weekend home @ Gotham. SUNDAYS at 7:30PM $5.00

In this hilarious interactive comedy, the audience is part of the show.  As "invited guests" the audience begins the evening witnessing the holy nuptials. Following the ceremony, a rousing reception takes place at Vinnie Black's Coliseum.  Dancing, champagne toasts, a full pasta dinner and of course, a slice of the wedding cake are provided by the Nunzio and Vitale "families".    Click on this link for other cities that Tony n' Tina's Wedding is playing!

Dazzling special effects highlight this tale of an American hero's struggle to tame heaven's own power.  This thrilling play for families culminates on a stormy night with the crack of thunder, a blinding flash of lightning and an experiment that changed the world!

Jesse, alienated from the pragmatism of his family and rural Virginia culture, draws and dreams of becoming something special. Leslie, the new girl from the city and the ultimate outsider, opens up a world of imagination, art and literature for him. Together they create Terabithia, a fantasy kingdom where they are safe from those who don't understand them. Their friendship grows as Jesse's world expands. When tragedy strikes, the strength gained in Terabithia lets Jesse move forward on his own, and lets him share the magic of his dreams.     Preteen/Young Adult Series.

Acclaimed as the debut of the year by one of the most exciting new writers in the country, Circle Mirror Transformation is the hilarious, moving new comedy about five citizens of a rural town who begin a community acting class, each with their own expectations, but soon learn more about each other and themselves than they bargained for. Circle Mirror Transformation has been hailed as one of the most insightful and original new plays of the year.

Marie is a pretty little girl with a pretty big heart. When the orphaned Marie is adopted by a regiment of the French soldiers, laughter erupts. The heartwarming story is filled with catchy tuneful music, two handfuls of tenor high C's and one energetic singing tomboy.
Choreography:  Jean Coralli & Jules Perrot  Music:  Adolphe Adam

Be sure to check out our Annual Fall Gala where the stars always come out to play! Join us for a spectacular evening of performances, music, dinner, dancing, and fun with Company artists and special surprise guests. Highlights include an exciting live and silent auction, and much, much more! All benefits support our award-winning Education Program.

Celebrate a revolutionary weekend! Our free, ever-popular reading of the Declaration of Independence features some of the most stirring words of political rhetoric ever written, spoken out loud by S&Co. actors and special guests from the community.

Ringing in the New Year with more laughs than should be legal, audiences will delight in the hilarious The Mystery of Irma Vep.  This zany romp through the mysterious and the sublime features two actors, eight roles (cue cross-dressing number), and wields a healthy mix of storytelling genres, from Hitchcock to Victorian melodrama to lurid, 19th century pulp fiction (or, in British parlance, 'penny dreadfuls'). This OBIE Award-winning, madcap escapade is sure to leave you breathless with laughter, while its expertly constructed story manages to both send-up and celebrate the traditional Gothic mystery.

The Declaration of Independence is preceded this year by Revolutionary Moments, a special collection of vignettes compiled by Tina Packer and featuring S&Co. actors. Part performance, part narration, part discussion, Revolutionary Moments highlights the influence of Shakespeare on some of history's most fascinating figures at key moments of decision. Not to be missed!
Karen Akers in Akers Sings Porter Anything Goes.

Annie is a spunky Depression-era orphan determined to find her parents, who abandoned her years ago on the doorstep of a New York City orphanage. This family favorite features the classic songs "Tomorrow," "It's A Hard Knock Life," "You're Never Fully Dressed Without A Smile," and "A New Deal For Christmas." As long as Annie is around, the sun will always come out tomorrow!     Season tickets on sale in June.

Join all your favorite barn-yard characters for the classic tale of Charlotte's Web by E.B. White. On the Zuckerman farm, a prancing, playful pig named Wilbur is the runt of the litter and could be the main course for Christmas dinner. Determined to save her friend, a gray spider named Charlotte spins a web that just might convince the farmer that Wilbur is very special. The whole family will love this tale of friendship and loyalty!      Season tickets on sale in June.

Fall down the rabbit hole into Disney's Alice and Wonderland Jr. Join Alice's madcap adventures as she chases the White Rabbit, races the Dodo Bird, gets tied up with the Tweedles, raps with a bubble-blowing Caterpillar, and beats the Queen of Hearts at her own game. Featuring such Disney classics as "I'm Late," "The Un-birthday Song" and "Zip-A-Dee-Doo-Dah," this is one important date you don't want to miss.      Season tickets on sale in June.

DCT's acclaimed National Tour returns to DCT in this hilarious musical sequel to Click, Clack Moo: Cows That Type. Duck turns the barnyard upside-down when Farmer Brown leaves his city-slicker brother Bob in charge of the farm. Giggle, Giggle, Quack is a madcap musical mutiny with Duck on the loose!

To Kill a Mockingbird follows the journey of Jem and Scout Finch, whose father, Atticus, has been appointed to defend a black man unjustly accused. As the trial progresses, the children witness the moral and societal issues that plague their town. To Kill a Mockingbird is a great reminder of the power of tolerance, courage and justice.     Season tickets on sale in June.

You'll swear "he's" back in the building! Nationally recognized Elvis tribute artist and winner of ABC's "The Next Best Thing," Trent Carlini, combines his uncanny resemblance and incredible vocal ability in a performance that will electrify you. In his most powerful tribute yet to the 'King of Rock and Roll,' Carlini will take viewers on a retrospective of Elvis Presley's career, from his unforgettable Rock-a-billy session, through the movie years, his `68 comeback period and the Las Vegas years of the `70s. With multiple costume changes, unbelievable visual media and more than 25 different hits, Trent Carlini truly showcases the King's exciting life in entertainment.

Performance tributes are a true Las Vegas art form, and "American Superstars" doesn't disappoint, with a talented cast including Britney Spears, Carrie Underwood, Elvis, Tim McGraw, Michael Jackson channelers.  The full-scale production show features dance routines and a quality band to back up the doppelgangers of music today and years gone by.  Group rates are also available for the show.  Please check lineup of acts before purchasing tickets.  Lineup subject to change without notice.
Catch this great tribute act as they perform the music of and impersonate the look of the legendary Beatles.

Big Elvis performs all the hits of the King of Rock & Roll, as well as some other popular tunes in the genres of Rock, Country, Gospel, R & B, and Pop spanning 6 decades of music. Big Elvis interacts with his audience, invites them to participate in his show and performs their requests, often including not just popular, but also obscure songs. More than 60 artifacts spanning nearly 10,000 years from one of the most significant sites in Virginia Indian history are on display for the first time in a museum setting. **1. Identify Entity Types:**
Looking at the columns, I can identify three main entity types:
*   **Show/Performance:** Attributes describing the event itself (name, dates, synopsis, type, links).
*   **Theater/Venue:** Attributes describing the location where the event takes place (name, address, city, state, zip, phone).
*   **Ticket/Pricing:** Attributes describing the cost and purchasing info (price, phone - though phone is often venue-specific, price is specific to the show instance).

**2. Analyze Attribute Grouping:**

    *   `endDate`: End date of the show.
    *   `type`: Type of performance (e.g., Solo Performance, Dance, Play).
    *   `sSynopsis`: Description of the show.
    *   `more`: Link to more info about the show.
    *   `sMoreInfo`: Link to specific performance info.
    *   `sTicketPrice`: Price of tickets for this specific show.

*   **Theater Attributes:**
    *   `theater`: Name of the theater.
    *   `sTheaterAddress`: Street address.
    *   `sTheaterCity`: City.
    *   `sTheaterState`: State.
    *   `sTheaterZip`: Zip code.
    *   `sTicketPhone`: Phone number (usually associated with the venue box office).

**3. Determine Splitting Strategy:**
The instruction states to split the table into multiple tables **ONLY if there is low overlap between attribute groups**. It also states this is **not database normalization**.

Let's look at the overlap.
*   The "Show" entity has attributes: `showName`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `type`, `sSynopsis`, `more`, `sMoreInfo`, `sTicketPrice`. (8 attributes)
*   The "Theater" entity has attributes: `theater`, `sTheaterAddress`, `sTheaterCity`, `sTheaterState`, `sTheaterZip`, `sTicketPhone`. (6 attributes)

In a strict normalization process, we would split these because a Theater hosts many Shows (1:N relationship). However, the prompt says "This is not database normalization" and to split only if there is "low overlap".

In this specific flat table, every row represents a specific *instance* of a show at a specific theater. The attributes are tightly coupled in the source data. For example, `sTicketPrice` is specific to the show instance, but `sTicketPhone` is specific to the theater.

Usually, in schema integration tasks like this (often based on schema matching literature), if the attributes clearly belong to distinct conceptual entities (like a Person and their Address, or a Product and its Category), and those entities have multiple attributes each, splitting is preferred to create a cleaner semantic model, even if it's not strictly normalized for a relational DB. While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. | from 10.5 to 75.0   | http://www.hoorwa.org                        |      60 | http://www.bikereg.com//inc/content/images/EventLogos/12569.png | Bennington        | <div><b>You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. </b></div>  <div><b><br></b></div>  <style>@font-face {  font-family: "Times";  }@font-face {  font-family: "Cambria";  }p.MsoNormal, li.MsoNormal, div.MsoNormal { margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: "Times New Roman"; }a:link, span.MsoHyperlink { color: blue; text-decoration: underline; }a:visited, span.MsoHyperlinkFollowed { color: purple; text-decoration: underline; }div.Section1 { page: Section1; }</style>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This year will mark the 7<sup>th</sup>  year of this increasingly popular event.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic  River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research  and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association <a href="http://www.hoorwa.org/">http://www.hoorwa.org</a>. For the last six years  riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic  and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new  routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have  seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great  theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great  getaway weekend. <i>Again this year the  venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington,  Vermont. </i><span> </span>Like last year, we  will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads  with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of  hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same  as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Each group  of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York  countryside.<span>  </span>Last year was the  first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this  will be offered again, and again. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Two State Tour<br></span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Stay tuned for more route details;  there may be some changes.</span></b></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The  Bridges and Monument  Loop</span></b></p>  <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument  and thru 3 covered bridges</span>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>RIDE DETAILS</b> </div>  <div><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Aid Station Items:</span> Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations.  <span style="text-decoration: underline;">Post Ride Picnic:</span> Food, beverages, baked goods and more. </div>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>THE COST:</b> This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! <img src="/inc/Editor_Files/images/emsmile.gif" align="absmiddle" border="0">.)</div>  <div><br></div>  <div>Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.<br></div>  <div><br></div>  <div><br></div> | VT      | 8/20/2011  | 7th Annual Hoosic River Ride                  | http://www.bikereg.com/events/register.asp?eventid=12569 |

Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. Psychology and Art professors Bettina Spencer and Krista Hoefle collaborate to curate an exhibition that seeks to present different and varying representation strategies and methods artists and scholars are using to investigate themes of war, violence, and reconciliation. The curators hope to create an aesthetic and intellectual environment that encourages empathy and solidarity in the face of a polarizing issue.

Featuring:
• Paintings by Donald Cameron
• Paintings and drawings by Dan Mills
• Video and photography installation by Shannon Benine
• New Media installation by Joseph DeLappe
• Ceramic sculpture by Paul Kuharic
• Sculpture by Dorothy Schultz

Presented by the Department of Art.

While David Auburn’s Proof is most certainly about mathematics at its core it is about people. Of its 2000 premiere John Simon wrote: “All four (characters) - whether loving, hating, encouraging or impeding one another - are intensely alive, complex, funny, human.” This cerebral mystery approaches issues such as what the link may be between genius and madness and whether either or both can be inherited. It is a story about human relationships, suggesting that developing trust and love can be as difficult, and just as uncertain, as establishing the truth of a mathematical proof.

You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

Carter, his wife, Sara, and her sister Maybelle at the dawn of the age of country music - an age they helped establish beginning in 1927. And they did it right here where the Carter Fold is today, in Poor Valley, at the foot of the Clinch Mountain in Southwest Virginia.
A Saturday with us in rural southwest Virginia will supply you with an evening of musical entertainment and country hospitality you won't soon forget. Chances are you'll make some new friends and take with you some fond memories. We'd love to have you visit us.

The Floyd Country Store, home of the Friday Night Jamboree, was constructed around 1910, and has been an important part of the community ever since. What is still most striking in the store though, is that as people walk through the door they cant help but smile.
The Jamboree starts every Friday at 6:30pm with an hour of bluegrass gospel music. At 7:30pm, dancers hit the floor, flatfooting and clogging to the music of regional Bluegrass or Old-Time bands. The music and dancing continues until at least 10:30pm, with an occasional two-step, square dance, or waltz thrown in for fun. If the crowd is willing, at 10:30pm we'll round up one of the jamming groups that can be found picking outside or upstairs in the store, and they will play for the crowd until around 11:30pm.
Admission is only $5. You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

There will be  well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road  and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all  aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech  support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with  bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support  your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at  registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until  3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times; font-weight: bold;">If you  register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee</span><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">. Commemorative ride jerseys are  available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr.  HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.   </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">THE 2011 ROUTES</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">: Named to honor the Ride’s founder  and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to  Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse  University crew team. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">Lisa’s Three Challenge: </span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This<b> </b>75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride. </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">This figure  eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the  4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on  this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route  includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of  stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain  you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and  its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well  as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of  descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!</span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"> </span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">The Hoosic 50</span></b><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;"></span></p>  <p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times;">It's just  that. Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations.  <span style="text-decoration: underline;">Post Ride Picnic:</span> Food, beverages, baked goods and more. </div>  <div><br></div>  <div><b>THE COST:</b> This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. You CAN REGISTER DAY OF--COME TO SOUTHERN VT COLLEGE AT LEAST 1/2 HOUR PRIOR TO RIDE START TIME. 

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.

 

The  Bridges and Monument Loop

The popular eight mile family ride that goes by the Bennington Monument and thru 3 covered bridges

RIDE DETAILS 
Aid Station Items: Oranges, Bananas, watermelon, Cytomax, Water, caffeinated soda (at last station), peanut butter and jelly, brownies, pretzels, cookies (fig and chocolate chip). Participants should carry at least 16 oz. Of fluid upon departure—whether in bottles or hydration packs, and a quick snack in case you get hungry between aid stations. Post Ride Picnic: Food, beverages, baked goods and more. 

THE COST: This event is entirely organized and run by volunteers and all proceeds after costs associated with running a fun and safe event go directly to HooRWA's programs. Registration fees will remain as posted here until August 1: after this date the price of the ride will increase by $10 and on ride morning an additional $5 will be levied (can you tell we are trying to get you to pre-register?).  For example, instead of $40 for the Two State tour on or prior to Aug. 1, you'll pay $50 if you register online by August 20 and $55 the day of the ride. (We've done our research and feel that this pricing scheme is very competitive with other rides of this nature. A great deal for a good cause! .)

Group Discount: We are offering groups of 5 or more who register together discounted fee of $35 per rider.

Jesse, alienated from the pragmatism of his family and rural Virginia culture, draws and dreams of becoming something special. Leslie, the new girl from the city and the ultimate outsider, opens up a world of imagination, art and literature for him. Together they create Terabithia, a fantasy kingdom where they are safe from those who don't understand them. Their friendship grows as Jesse's world expands. When tragedy strikes, the strength gained in Terabithia lets Jesse move forward on his own, and lets him share the magic of his dreams.     Preteen/Young Adult Series.

Circle Mirror Transformation has been hailed as one of the most insightful and original new plays of the year.

Ringing in the New Year with more laughs than should be legal, audiences will delight in the hilarious The Mystery of Irma Vep.  This zany romp through the mysterious and the sublime features two actors, eight roles (cue cross-dressing number), and wields a healthy mix of storytelling genres, from Hitchcock to Victorian melodrama to lurid, 19th century pulp fiction (or, in British parlance, 'penny dreadfuls'). This OBIE Award-winning, madcap escapade is sure to leave you breathless with laughter, while its expertly constructed story manages to both send-up and celebrate the traditional Gothic mystery.

Not to be missed!

During his renditions of Elvis ballards Big Elvis shows his warm heart and bares his soul to the extent that there is not a dry eye in the room.

Country Superstars Tribute, a fast-paced, concert style event, features a world-class live five-piece band and tribute artists to some of the biggest names in country music history, such as Willie Nelson, Garth Brooks, Tim McGraw, Reba McEntire, Kenny Chesney and more! BODIES...The Exhibition, which showcases real full-bodies and organs, provides a detailed, three-dimensional vision of the human form rarely seen outside of an anatomy lab or a morgue. The Exhibition showcases 13 whole-body specimens and more than 260 organs and partial body specimens. These real human bodies have been meticulously dissected, preserved through an innovative process and respectfully presented, giving visitors the opportunity to view the beauty and complexity of their own organs and systems.

The 25,000-square-foot exhibit features numerous items from the Titanic, including luggage, the ship's whistles, floor tiles from the first-class smoking room, a window frame from the Verandah Cafe and an unopened bottle of champagne with a 1900 vintage. In addition, the exhibit features a piece of Titanic's hull, a full-scale re-creation of the Grand Staircase as well as a newly expanded outer Promenade Deck, complete with the frigid temperatures felt on that fateful April night.    These actual artifacts, recovered from two and one half miles below the surface of the North Atlantic, tell the story behind the legendary Titanic's short journey from construction and destruction to eventual recovery. Walk her decks, peer into her cabins and meet her passengers and crew.    Described as a floating palace, the incomparable Titanic was deemed "practically unsinkable" by the White Star Line and its builders. However, on a calm April night in 1912, the massive luxury liner struck an iceberg and slowly sank into the North Atlantic. Since then, many items from the wreckage have been recovered and added to Titanic: The Artifact Exhibition.     The personal artifacts on display offer haunting, emotional connections to the forever-altered lives of those on board the Titanic. Visitors even have a chance to walk through authentically re-created first- and third-class rooms, with furnishings by original manufacturers.

The repertoire is going to be extraordinary...a mix of timeless Hollywood classics, along with all the favorites that her fans like to hear her sing. Marvel at the breathtaking spectacle of animals brought to life by a cast of more than 40 actors. Featuring such hits as "Sherry," "Big Girls Don't Cry," "Can't Take My Eyes Off You," "Oh, What a Night," and more, "Jersey Boys" will have you singing along just like the crowds of Broadway

More than 60 artifacts spanning nearly 10,000 years from one of the most significant sites in Virginia Indian history are on display for the first time in a museum setting. Werowocomoco was the principal residence of Powhatan, paramount chief of 30-some Indian tribes in Virginias coastal region at the time English colonists arrived in 1607. Archaeological excavations have revealed not only that the York River site was a uniquely important place during Powhatans time, but also that its role as a political and social center predated the Powhatan chiefdom. Werowocomoco is the place where Captain John Smith was taken prisoner by Powhatan in 1607 and first met Powhatans daughter Pocahontas.
